==Problem==
The instructions on a <imath>350</imath>-gram bag of coffee beans say that proper brewing of a large mug of pour-over coffee requires <imath>20</imath> grams of coffee beans. What is the greatest number of properly brewed large mugs of coffee that can be made from the coffee beans in that bag?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 16 \qquad\textbf{(B) } 17 \qquad\textbf{(C) } 18 \qquad\textbf{(D) } 19 \qquad\textbf{(E) } 20</imath>

==Solution 1==
<imath>\frac{350}{20}</imath> is <imath>17.5</imath>. We round down to find the maximum he can make (he cannot brew half of a cup), so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 17}</imath>.

==Solution 2==
We can use <imath>340</imath>-grams if we use <imath>17</imath> mugs. This is because <imath>20 \cdot 17 = 340</imath>. We cannot use <imath>18</imath> because that would mean using <imath>360</imath>-grams. The answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 17}</imath>.

Note that you can also find this by finding <imath>\lfloor \frac{350}{20} \rfloor = 17.</imath>

~lprado

==Solution 3==
Dividing <imath>350</imath> by <imath>20</imath>, we get <imath>17</imath> with a remainder of <imath>10</imath>. However, <imath>10</imath> grams cannot make a properly brewed large mug of coffee, as stated in the problem. We can only count fully brewed mugs of coffee, hence the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 17}</imath>.

~Yoonyoung11
~Minor edits and Latex by Yvz2900

==Solution 4 - Cheese (Sort of)==
We multiply <imath>20</imath> by each of the answer choices to see if we can find which one is closest and under <imath>350.</imath> First, we try solution <imath>\text{A}</imath>, which is <imath>16</imath>. <imath>16 \cdot 20 = 320,</imath> which is <imath>30</imath> off from 350, so <imath>\text{A}</imath> cannot be the answer, because we can add another <imath>20</imath>. Moving on to answer choice <imath>\text{B},</imath> <imath>17 \cdot 20 = 340.</imath> We notice that <imath>350-340=10,</imath> and so we cannot add another <imath>20</imath> to get closer but less than <imath>350.</imath> (The next number, <imath>18</imath>, would result in <imath>20 \cdot 18=360,</imath> which is more than <imath>350</imath>.) So, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 17}</imath>.

(note - the actual cheese solution would likely include every single answer choice, but I use a bit of intellect in this solution)
